- Does routing to Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) vs. Hosted API change the BAA requirement?

Hi Ava — thanks for the clear diagram and the great questions. Short answers up front: 

- Yes, if the payload includes patient identifiers tied to health information (names, MRNs, DOBs, clinical notes), that is PHI under HIPAA and typically triggers a BAA when Redwood is providing processing services on those data.
- Using Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) or a Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) changes the operational control and data residency model and can reduce legal concerns for some customers, but it does not by itself negate the need for a BAA if Redwood is processing PHI on behalf of MediLoop.
- Preprocessing in your environment that strips direct identifiers and only sends de-identified tokens/text reduces scope, but the devil is in the details — we and your legal team will want to validate the de-identification technique (expert determination or safe harbor).

I'm looping in Monica (our PM for Compliance) and Rishi (security lead) to provide our standard BAA draft and confirm technical controls. I'll attach the BAA draft and a short note on controls in a follow-up.

Next steps proposal: 
1) We share Redwood_BAA_Draft_v1.pdf for your legal to review.
2) Technical call with your architects to walk the routing diagram and discuss de-id approaches (30-45m).
3) If MediLoop needs Dedicated or Private, we can scope an initial Proof-of-Concept deployment config and include it in the SOW.

Can your legal ops team do an initial pass this week?

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Ava — Monica from Product Compliance here. Adding a few specifics from the compliance checklist to help your legal/security team triage quickly: 

- BAA scope: Our standard BAA covers processing of PHI while Redwood acts as a Business Associate. The BAA includes permitted uses, obligations around safeguards, breach notification timelines, and assistance with patient requests where applicable.
- Data segregation: For Hosted API we have tenant isolation and encryption at rest and in transit; Dedicated and Private deployments offer additional isolation and customer-managed key options (KMS/HSM).
- Access controls & logging: We provide role-based access controls, audit logs with per-request metadata, and can surface token-level audit data on request for SOC evidence.
- Retention & deletion: The BAA allows customers to specify retention windows; we support automated purge policies and can provide attestation for deletion events.

A couple of clarifying questions for your diagram: 
1) Where does the de-id step occur? (client-side pre-processor or inside your staging environment?)
2) Do you plan to send full clinical notes or extractive summaries?

If you prefer, we can redline the attached BAA with two options: (A) Hosted API + PSAs around de-id best practices (narrow SCOPES), or (B) Dedicated/Private + expanded SLA and physical security language. Let us know which path you prefer and we'll prepare a redline.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Product Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
